problem.title: Bell inequalities for long-range vacuum correlations

question.summary: Vacuum entanglement persists at arbitrary separation, but direct CHSH violation by bounded distant regions has not been proved or excluded.
question.importance: The problem separates long-range vacuum entanglement from Bell nonlocality that localized observers can test. It probes the operational content of correlations in algebraic quantum field theory.
question.unresolved: Prove a direct CHSH violation at arbitrarily large distance, or prove Bell locality beyond a finite separation.

claims.title: Arbitrary-distance harvesting reveals hidden nonlocality
claims.text: Reznik, Retzker and Silman obtain entanglement at arbitrary separation. Their detector state violates CHSH only after local filtering and postselection, not directly.

decisions.rationale: Status assessed against the archived statement in the 2026-08-12 primary-source audit; the evidence ledger lists the results considered.

editorial.interpretation: Entanglement, failure of a PPT analogue and postselected hidden nonlocality are weaker than the direct bounded-region CHSH statement in the archived problem.
